title: Heuristic sketches for PR risk and quick triage
content:
Purpose: fast mental model + tiny rubric for triaging incoming PRs when I'm the reviewer on-call. Not a checklist for thorough reviews — more a quick filter and note-taking scratchpad for follow-ups.

Notes to self / heuristics (sketch form):
- First 60s: read title + first comment + changed files list. Is this: patch, refactor, security, infra, rollback? classify quickly.
- If > 10 files changed and majority are non-docs -> escalate to full review (high friction).
- Hot paths: anything touching serving runtime core (request pipeline, batching, kv cache, kernel selection) gets +3 risk. These are latency-safety areas.
- Config-only changes -> usually low risk (unless feature flags removed/defaults changed).
- Tests changed? No tests = +2 risk. Bad tests (flake-prone) = +1. Good unit + integration coverage = -1.
- Size heuristic: lines changed / critical-file flag -> very rough multiplier. e.g., 1-50 lines low, 50-500 moderate, >500 large. But context > raw numbers.

Quick signal checklist (one-liners to scribble):
- Does CI include e2e against a local-ish env (docker-compose / dev cluster)? Y/N
- Are runtime benchmarks affected (seq-len path)? Y/N/Unclear
- Are new feature-flags present (and are defaults safe)? Note flag name.
- Is there a canary or rollout plan in the PR description? (route to console rollout config)
- Does PR change public API (REST/SDK surface or inference contract)? If yes, add stakeholder tag.
- Rollback path documented? If not, ask dev to add.

Lightweight PR risk score (use for triage, 0..10):
- Base = 1
- core-serving-touch: +3 if touching runtime core/kv/cache/batching/kernels
- tests: -1 if good tests, +2 if zero tests
- infra-config: +2 if changes infra defaults or helm/kustomize manifests
- lines: +1 if >200 lines (code), +2 if >1000
- public-api: +2
- migration: +2 if DB or on-disk format/serialized state
- urgency: +1 if bugfix to production incident
- author-experience: -1 if author has previous high-quality PRs in area
Examples:
- small typo in docs: base 1, docs-only -> score 0-1 -> low priority
- KV cache bugfix (no tests): base1 +3(core) +2(no-tests) +1(>200 lines) = 7 -> high, require SRE/owner ping, add canary

What to ask in first-review comment (templates):
- Short safety request: "Could you add explicit rollback steps for this change and a simple canary plan? Example: route 5% to old model variant for 1 hour, metrics X/Y/Z checked."
- Testing ask: "Can you add a small integration test that exercises the altered code path with a cached/un-cached sequence?"
- Observability ask: "Add a trace span around <function> and a tag that identifies this deployment so we can filter post-rollout."

Follow-ups to capture in PR body or my own TODOs:
- Add a small perf microbenchmark if kernel selection logic changed.
- Add a regression eval prompt set if any generation output heuristics changed (tokenization, format).
- Coordinate release note: performance change or deprecation.
- Schedule a brief sync with the Solutions Eng owner if this changes customer-facing latencies.

Quick mental models and gotchas specific to serving-runtime:
- KV cache changes are high-impact but often small diffs. Always confirm cache key format + TTL semantics. A bug there corrupts coherency across requests.
- Batching edge cases: changes that assume fixed sequence lengths usually break when a new model with different context length is rolled. Flag them.
- Quantization/config knobs: ensure fallback path still exists for unquantized model variants; check routing policy compatibility.

Small checklist to paste in PR (copyable):
- [ ] Rollback steps documented
- [ ] Canary/rollout plan included
- [ ] Instrumentation/trace added for critical path
- [ ] Unit + integration tests cover the change
- [ ] Stakeholders cc'd (SRE, product owner, solutions eng if public API)

Rough personal SLA for review pipeline (how I triage when paged):
- If score <= 2: skim + approve in 1-2 hours
- If 3-5: deeper review, ask questions, require CI green + at least 1 written e2e result (same day)
- If >=6: block merge until owner replies and we have a canary + rollback plan (treat as high-risk)

Scratch ideas (to iterate into a small tooling script):
- A tiny GH bot that computes the score from file paths and labels PR with risk:low/med/high. Heuristic config in repo for exceptions.
- Auto-insert checklist template into PR when touched files include packages/runtime/* or serving/*
- Dev command `dev rollback-plan` that outputs a checklist with required console steps (route %, monitor metrics, revert image) based on changed files.

Open questions for follow-up:
- How often do we actually run stress/perf for merged kernel changes? Can we automate a nightly perf job for master?
- Should we enforce a minimal canary for all runtime core changes via merge gate?

Notes-to-self: next time I review a KV change, record the exact tracing IDs and example keys that failed during local repro and attach to PR.

End of scratchpad.
